selection: step-out from bonsai1/L35/N4245- (10x queue, model pilot: sonnet)

neighbours.label: the word naming a field or group right before 'jargon' (or similar: speak, terminology), where a jargon noun is predicted, plus the ' j' of jargon itself after such a modifier
fire: Reading the textbook, I kept stumbling over the dense financial jargon that assumed years of prior study.
My uncle is a pilot and tends to drop aviation jargon into every dinner conversation.
The manual explains the setup, but the engineering jargon in chapter three will lose most readers.
Doctors who skip medical jargon get better trust ratings from their patients.
Her thesis is full of academic jargon, which is fine for specialists but hard for everyone else.
Teenagers invent internet jargon so fast that parents cannot keep up.
Fans of the sport throw around coaching jargon like 'zone blitz' without explaining it.
The support agent switched from technical jargon to simple language once he noticed my confusion.
quiet: Reading the textbook, I kept stumbling over the dense financial tables that assumed years of prior study.
My uncle is a pilot and tends to drop stories about his flights into every dinner conversation.
The manual explains the setup, but the engineering diagrams in chapter three will lose most readers.
Doctors who skip long appointments get worse trust ratings from their patients.
Her thesis is full of academic citations, which is fine for specialists but hard for everyone else.
Teenagers invent new songs so fast that parents cannot keep up.
Fans of the sport throw around nicknames like 'Big Easy' without explaining them.
The support agent switched from reading a script to speaking naturally once he noticed my confusion.

notes: Model pilot (sonnet arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L35/N4245- (zeroing this neuron removes 0.87 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Sonnet 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Probes: ' j' of jargon fired 0.73-0.95; the field word before 'terminology' and 'speak' was weak (0.05-0.19), and 'legal' alone fired 0.43 before a non-jargon noun, so I avoided 'legal' in the quiet set. I made the label mainly 'jargon' after a field modifier, and near misses keep the field word with a different noun.
